summary.oneLiner: ARIS is building a technology-led orchestration layer that brings structure, visibility, and control to India's fragmented construction procurement ecosystem.
summary.business: Arisinfra Solutions Limited operates a B2B digital platform that aggregates demand, connects it to a distributed vendor network, and manages procurement, delivery, documentation, and credit in real time. The company serves developers, contractors, and suppliers across India, transforming manual, transaction-driven construction procurement into a coordinated, data-driven system. ARIS also provides contract manufacturing supply assurance and a Developer-as-a-Service (DaaS) execution model for landowners and real estate developers.

currentContext.strengths: Asset-light, scalable platform model with network effects from a pan-India vendor and customer base.|Proprietary technology stack digitizing price discovery, RFQs, order processing, vendor allocation, documentation, compliance, credit decisions, and logistics.|Structural supply control and margin expansion through 9+ million MTPA of reserved contract manufacturing capacity, creating a competitive barrier.|Deliberate portfolio shift away from low-margin traded commodities (steel/cement) to higher-margin, execution-critical categories (aggregates, RMC, asphalt).|High repeat order rate (78%) and integrated DaaS model yielding 55–60% EBITDA margins with exclusive materials supply relationships.
currentContext.strategies: Build a technology-led procurement and supply orchestration platform that offers price discovery, vendor aggregation, delivery reliability, and working capital tools to capture a disproportionate share of industry formalisation benefits.|Expand into execution-critical categories such as asphalt, bringing technology-led visibility and supply reliability to an underpenetrated segment.|Leverage AI and data-driven platforms to reduce inefficiency across the construction value chain, including real-time price discovery, vendor management, delivery tracking, credit risk assessment, and project reporting.|Position as an integrated partner for developers and infrastructure players, managing material supply, project coordination, working capital, delivery monitoring, and sales support beyond traditional procurement.|The Board has approved a Dividend Distribution Policy as per Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The policy lists key factors that may affect the decision to pay out earnings in the form of dividends, indicating a structured, principle-based approach to capital allocation.
currentContext.expansion: Arisinfra operates an asset-light model and does not own manufacturing assets. Its capacity expansion is driven by securing long-term reserved capacity through partner plants under its Contract Manufacturing segment. As of FY 2025-26, total reserved capacity reached 9 Million+ MTPA, comprising 6.1 million MT in Aggregates, 2.7 million MT in Ready-Mix Concrete, and 0.3 million MT in Asphalt. The company plans to deepen this network of plant relationships across these categories to strengthen supply assurance and margin expansion. Additionally, the Developer-as-a-Service (DaaS) segment was formally launched in FY 2025-26 with 9 active projects spanning approximately 2 million square feet and an estimated Gross Development Value of ₹1,200 Crore+, with live execution underway, representing a structural expansion of the company's role in the construction value chain.
currentContext.mdna: India's infrastructure pipeline of ₹213 trillion+ across 14,500+ NIP projects provides a long-dated, visible demand runway for construction materials and execution services.|Government capital expenditure is expected to remain elevated as a percentage of GDP through FY 2027-28, supporting sustained demand.|The premiumisation of residential real estate (homes above ₹1 crore now 50% of sales) increases material consumption per unit, supporting long-term demand for value-added construction products.|Increasing formalisation under RERA and the growing share of organised developers (60-65% of new launches) drive adoption of organised procurement and demand for reliable, technology-enabled supply partners.|Sustained residential launches across major metropolitan markets (MMR, NCR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad) provide a broad-based demand environment.

risks.note: High likelihood and high impact; customers may delay or default on payments, with receivable cycles often longer than payable cycles, creating cash flow strain.
54% of revenue from Maharashtra and 29% from Tamil Nadu creates susceptibility to regional regulatory, political, or climate disruptions.
A few large vendors contribute a significant share of supplies, and vendors may fail to supply consistently, causing quality or delivery issues that affect fulfilment.
Misalignment between receivable and payable cycles creates cash flow challenges, exacerbated by high-growth operations.
Well-funded new entrants may erode market share or compress margins, threatening the company's position in the construction materials procurement space.
Stakeholders may be slow to adopt digital procurement tools, potentially limiting the scalability and efficiency gains of the platform.
Changes in GST, environmental, or mining regulations could affect sourcing, pricing, or operational viability.

one-line thesis: Arisinfra delivered a structural inflection in FY26 with 39% revenue growth and 10x PAT expansion to INR 60 Cr, driven by a shift toward higher-margin Contract Manufacturing (47% mix) and the high-visibility DAAS model. The key catalyst is the transition to multi-year secured capacity (INR 6,000+ Cr visibility over 5 years) via refundable deposits, which de-risks volume while maintaining an asset-light balance sheet (Net Debt/Equity -0.09x).
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,068 Cr (+39% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 343 Cr (+55% YoY). EBITDA: INR 101 Cr (+100% YoY), Margin 9.43% (+290 bps); Q4 EBITDA INR 31 Cr (+202% YoY), Margin 8.8% (impacted by one-offs). PAT: INR 60 Cr (vs INR 6 Cr prior year); Q4 PAT INR 22 Cr (vs loss prior year). Order Book: DAAS pipeline INR 1,800+ Cr GDV (12+ projects); Secured Contract Manufacturing visibility INR 6,000+ Cr over 5 years. Net Debt: Negative (-0.09x D/E); Cash flow from ops INR 142 Cr. One-offs: INR 5 Cr expected credit loss provision in Q4; INR 5 Cr non-cash unwinding income on financial instruments (deposits) impacting reported EBITDA.
guidance: Revenue growth: 35-40% CAGR for FY27/FY28. EBITDA Margin: Sustained 10-10.5% (sweet spot), with potential upside from mix shift. Order Inflow: Targeting 85-90% of annual top-line secured in Q1 FY27. Capex/Commissioning: INR 25-50 Cr incremental investment in refundable capacity deposits in FY27.
order book & pipeline: DAAS: INR 1,800+ Cr GDV under execution (12+ projects). Contract Manufacturing: INR 4,000-4,500 Cr visibility from current deposit base + INR 800 Cr Capacite contract (5-year tenure); Total 5-year visibility >INR 6,000 Cr. Annualized Contract Mfg capacity: 9 Mn metric tons (targeting INR 700-800 Cr revenue at 75-80% utilization).
segment / subsidiary detail: B2B Supply: 44% of FY26 rev, entry point for network density. Contract Manufacturing: 47% of rev, +169% YoY growth in Q4, volumes +91% YoY to 11.29 LMT, utilization improved to 50% (Q4) from 39%. DAAS: 9% of rev, +264% YoY growth in Q4 to INR 36 Cr, higher margin profile.
growth verticals / optionality: Asphalt vertical launch (INR 30 Cr Q4 rev, +88% QoQ, 28 customers); Expansion of wallet share with existing large contractors (currently 5-50% penetration); Geographic deepening in existing 23 states; Potential adjacencies in construction chemicals (currently 2-3%).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 290 bps to 9.43% FY26. Q4 margin 8.8% suppressed by INR 5 Cr credit loss provision; normalized Q4 margin ~10.2%. Management targets steady-state 10-10.5% EBITDA margins. Cost control driven by tech-platform efficiency and volume discounts on raw materials; no commodity price risk (pass-through model).
capex / expansion: Asset-light model: No heavy manufacturing capex. Capital deployed as refundable security deposits to secure long-term capacity (INR 160 Cr cumulative in FY26). FY27 guidance: Additional INR 25-50 Cr in deposits. Deposits recognized as financial instruments with non-cash unwinding impacts.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Reinvestment into capacity deposits to secure 5-year revenue visibility. Priority 2: Working capital optimization (days reduced from 110 to 66). Priority 3: Funding bridge between payables/receivables (new INR 30 Cr WC limit sanctioned, targeting INR 100-150 Cr total). No dividend guidance; focus on compounding PAT and OCF.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on scaling asphalt and DAAS projects; Concentration risk in large contractor relationships (e.g., Capacite); Regulatory/Accounting changes on treatment of security deposits; Macro slowdown in real estate/infra affecting demand; Collection risk on legacy receivables (INR 40-42 Cr stuck, though improving).
management quality / tone: Highly confident and strategic; Emphasis on 'predictability' and 'visibility' over spot transactions; Disciplined on working capital and cost control; Aggressive on securing multi-year contracts early in the fiscal year (Q1 focus).
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 5 Cr 'unwinding income' is a non-cash accounting artifact from discounting long-term refundable deposits, which artificially suppresses reported EBITDA while cash flows remain robust. The business effectively operates as a 'capacity bank,' using small refundable deposits to lock in massive multi-year supply/demand matching without owning assets. Management aims to secure 85-90% of the full-year revenue target within the first quarter (Q1) via large anchor deals.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for predictable, large-scale material supply without heavy capex; Pressure on working capital in traditional EPC/Real Estate. | Capacite Infraprojects Ltd | beneficiary | High | Signed INR 800 Cr/5-year contract with Aris; gains secured capacity and pricing predictability for road/infra projects without owning quarries/plants. |
| Fragmented supply chain; lack of technology integration in procurement; working capital inefficiencies. | Large Real Estate Developers (Unlisted/Listed peers) | beneficiary | Med | Access to DAAS model for end-to-end project management and integrated procurement, reducing execution risk and improving cash cycles. |
| Traditional manufacturers face cyclical demand and pricing volatility; need for guaranteed offtake. | Contract Manufacturing Partners (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | Gain guaranteed long-term offtake agreements and capacity utilization stability via Aris's network. |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
